title: Functional antibody responses and protection against symptomatic dengue

analysis.scope_and_question: Exposure to dengue virus (DENV) triggers the development of anti-viral antibodies that may contribute to either protection or disease progression.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Antibodies exist in different isotypes and subtypes, with diverse specificities and functions.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: IgG antibodies are produced during primary and secondary DENV infections, where they play a role central role in mediating protective immunity, and may also contribute to antibody-dependent enhancement in a secondary heterotypic infection.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Although IgG antibodies are widely recognised as key mediators of protective immune responses during DENV infection, antibody specificities, types and functions that reliably correlate with protection remain unclear.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: A better understanding of anti-DENV antibodies and their roles in protection against symptomatic dengue is essential especially in guiding the design of dengue vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of antibody responses in dengue virus infection, focusing on their dual potential to protect against or exacerbate the disease. It highlights the importance of IgG antibodies in both protective immunity and antibody-dependent enhancement, particularly in secondary heterotypic infections. The review underscores the need for further research to identify specific antibody isotypes, subtypes, and functions that reliably correlate with protection. This understanding is critical for the development of effective dengue vaccines. The review also discusses the current state of knowledge on antibody functions and effector mechanisms, emphasizing the significance of naturally acquired immunity and neutralising antibody responses following vaccination.

title: Repeated-Dose High-Dose Ivermectin Pharmacokinetics and Safety in Children with Acute Dengue.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Ivermectin has shown anti-dengue virus activity in experimental systems, and an adult dengue trial found faster clearance of circulating non-structural protein 1 (NS1) without improvement in viremia or clinical outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Pediatric pharmacokinetic and safety data for repeated high-dose regimens remain limited. We characterized repeated-dose ivermectin pharmacokinetics and safety in children with acute uncomplicated dengue weighing ≥15 kg.
analysis.methods: In this prospective, open-label, sequential dose-escalation study, children aged 1-15 years who presented within 72 h of fever onset and met the protocol laboratory-confirmation criteria for dengue received ivermectin 400 or 600 μg/kg once daily for 3 days. Noncompartmental analyses estimated exposure and peak concentrations from intensive plasma sampling. Exploratory analyses examined associations between exposure and viremia and NS1 trajectories during the first 48 h after dose 1; the study was not designed or powered to evaluate antiviral efficacy.
analysis.main_results: All 24 children completed follow-up and experienced at least one adverse event; most events were consistent with acute dengue. Six participants (25%) experienced serious adverse events consisting of grade 4 neutropenia; all participants were clinically well, required no neutropenia-specific treatment, and showed improvement at the next available assessment or follow-up. One asymptomatic grade 1 QTc-prolongation adverse event was recorded and required no intervention. Exposure increased with dose: median 0-48-h area under the concentration-time curve (AUClast) was 1316.49 and 2129.41 ng·h/mL at 400 and 600 μg/kg, respectively, and corresponding maximum observed concentrations (Cmax) were 107.50 and 165.50 ng/mL.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Ivermectin in Pediatric Dengue Patients (PKIDEN) therefore fills an important dengue-specific pediatric clinical pharmacology gap and provides repeated-dose exposure and safety reference data that may inform dose selection, exposure interpretation, and safety monitoring in future studies. The study was not designed to determine antiviral efficacy or clinical benefit.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide repeated-dose exposure and safety reference data that may inform dose selection, exposure interpretation, and safety monitoring in future dengue studies. They also highlight the need for further research to evaluate antiviral efficacy and clinical benefit.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Analyses confined to the first 48 h identified no clear exposure-response association with viremia or NS1 trajectories. The evidence is moderate as the study focused on pharmacokinetics and safety rather than efficacy.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterize the repeated-dose pharmacokinetics and safety of ivermectin in children with acute uncomplicated dengue weighing ≥15 kg. A prospective, open-label, sequential dose-escalation study was conducted with 24 children aged 1-15 years who presented within 72 h of fever onset and had laboratory-confirmed dengue. Ivermectin was administered at doses of 400 or 600 μg/kg once daily for 3 days. Noncompartmental analyses were used to estimate exposure and peak concentrations, while exploratory analyses examined associations between exposure and viremia or NS1 trajectories. All participants experienced at least one adverse event, with six (25%) having serious events, including grade 4 neutropenia. One asymptomatic grade 1 QTc-prolongation event was recorded. Exposure increased with dose, but dose-normalized parameters showed no clear relationship with body weight. No exposure-response association was found with viremia or NS1 trajectories within the first 48 h. The study was not designed to evaluate antiviral efficacy or clinical benefit, but it fills an important gap in dengue-specific pediatric pharmacology by providing exposure and safety data. The evidence is moderate due to the study's focus on safety and pharmacokinetics rather than efficacy.

title: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify novel antiviral compounds from plant-derived natural products to address the unmet need for specific antiviral therapies against mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells.
analysis.methods: Functional assays were used to evaluate the antiviral activity of extracts, which led to the isolation and structural characterization of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins.
analysis.main_results: Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. The isolated compounds inhibited DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that spirostane saponins are promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These compounds could inform the development of new antiviral therapies for dengue and other arboviruses, potentially reducing the global health burden of these infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of a single DENV-2 strain and the lack of in vivo validation, which may affect the generalizability of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study identified spirostane saponins from Solanaceae plants as promising antiviral compounds against DENV-2, with potential for broad-spectrum antiviral therapy development.

title: Advanced next-generation vaccines for dengue and other flaviviral infections.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on dengue virus (DENV) and dengue disease, with an emphasis on developing next-generation vaccines. The central question is about the challenges and opportunities in creating scalable, non-infectious vaccine production platforms for dengue and other flaviviruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of methods and findings from 2018 to 2024, highlighting the development of DNA-based vaccine platforms. It describes the use of algorithmic overlap extension PCR (OE-PCR) and an improved technique, asymmetric extension supported by a simulator for oligonucleotide extension (AESOE), to create synthetic DNA constructs. Machine learning tools, including recurrent neural network-based amplification prediction and LAMP primer design, were integrated to enhance synthesis efficiency and expand applications for surveillance and diagnostics.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that recent advancements in nucleic acid-based immunogens have shown promise for scalable, non-infectious vaccine production. However, generating high-dose DNA constructs that can induce effective immune responses without live-virus propagation remains a significant challenge.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while live-virus-free strategies may enhance biosafety and reduce development timelines, the effectiveness of these DNA constructs in inducing robust immune responses is still under investigation. There is a lack of comprehensive data on the long-term efficacy and safety of these platforms in real-world settings.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that further research is needed to optimize DNA construct design and improve the scalability of these platforms. It also highlights the importance of expanding applications for surveillance and diagnostics using these technologies, particularly in resource-limited settings.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the development of next-generation vaccines for dengue virus, emphasizing the use of nucleic acid-based immunogens. It highlights the challenges in creating high-dose DNA constructs that can induce effective immune responses without live-virus propagation. The review describes the use of algorithmic overlap extension PCR (OE-PCR) and an improved technique, asymmetric extension supported by a simulator for oligonucleotide extension (AESOE), to assemble synthetic DNA fragments. Machine learning tools were integrated to enhance synthesis efficiency and expand applications for surveillance and diagnostics. While live-virus-free strategies offer potential benefits in biosafety and accessibility, the review identifies gaps in long-term efficacy and safety data. It suggests future research should focus on optimizing DNA construct design and improving scalability, particularly for resource-limited settings.

analysis.methods: The study uses climate modeling and epidemiological data to predict the potential impact of the El Niño event on dengue virus transmission. It also incorporates historical outbreak data and immunological surveys to assess the population's susceptibility.
analysis.main_results: The study reports that the upcoming El Niño event is likely to increase the risk of DENV-3 outbreaks in Latin America due to the population's low immunity levels. It highlights the need for immediate preparedness measures.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the El Niño event provides a narrow window for implementing preventive measures against DENV-3 outbreaks. This is a novel insight into the interplay between climate patterns and dengue disease dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for surveillance, vector control, and clinical preparedness in Latin America during the El Niño event. They emphasize the importance of differentiating DENV-3 outbreaks from other flaviviruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on predictive modeling and historical data, which may have limitations in capturing real-time transmission dynamics. However, the evidence is considered moderate due to the integration of multiple data sources.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the potential impact of the upcoming El Niño event on DENV-3 outbreaks in Latin America, where the population has limited immunity. The authors interpret that the El Niño event presents a critical opportunity for intervention, offering a novel perspective on climate-disease interactions. The findings have significant implications for public health planning, particularly in regions with low DENV-3 immunity. However, the study's reliance on predictive models and historical data limits the confidence in its conclusions, resulting in a moderate evidence assessment.

title: Optimal Control of Dengue under Vaccine Heterogeneity: From Dynamical Analysis to Dynamic Strategy Optimization.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of optimal dengue control under vaccine heterogeneity, particularly the differing protective efficacy between susceptible and recovered individuals and the risk of antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) increasing severe disease risk.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed a dengue transmission model incorporating ADE effects and time delays, and used it to derive the basic reproduction number and establish equilibrium stability conditions.
analysis.methods: An optimal control framework was developed that integrates vaccine heterogeneity into a composite objective functional, balancing health losses, secondary infection penalties, and intervention costs.
analysis.main_results: On a baseline calibrated to R 0 =1.515, three key findings were identified: targeted vaccination yields the lowest total societal cost while achieving health outcomes close to the ideal vaccine, the ideal vaccine is cost-dominant when its daily price remains below $1 per capita, and the risky vaccine incurs higher long-term costs due to ADE-driven late-stage health loss, despite its lower procurement price.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as providing quantitative guidance for vaccine selection under varying resource constraints, highlighting the importance of considering vaccine heterogeneity and ADE effects in dynamic strategy optimization.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform public health strategies for dengue control by offering a framework for selecting vaccines based on cost and health outcomes, particularly in resource-constrained settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the reliance on a calibrated baseline and the absence of real-world data, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence strength is moderate due to the theoretical nature of the model and the assumptions made.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of optimal dengue control under vaccine heterogeneity, particularly the differing protective efficacy between susceptible and recovered individuals and the risk of antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) increasing severe disease risk. The authors developed a dengue transmission model incorporating ADE effects and time delays, and used it to derive the basic reproduction number and establish equilibrium stability conditions. An optimal control framework was developed that integrates vaccine heterogeneity into a composite objective functional, balancing health losses, secondary infection penalties, and intervention costs. On a baseline calibrated to R 0 =1.515, three key findings were identified: targeted vaccination yields the lowest total societal cost while achieving health outcomes close to the ideal vaccine, the ideal vaccine is cost-dominant when its daily price remains below $1 per capita, and the risky vaccine incurs higher long-term costs due to ADE-driven late-stage health loss, despite its lower procurement price. The authors interpreted these findings as providing quantitative guidance for vaccine selection under varying resource constraints, highlighting the importance of considering vaccine heterogeneity and ADE effects in dynamic strategy optimization. These findings can inform public health strategies for dengue control by offering a framework for selecting vaccines based on cost and health outcomes, particularly in resource-constrained settings. The study's limitations include the reliance on a calibrated baseline and the absence of real-world data, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence strength is moderate due to the theoretical nature of the model and the assumptions made.

analysis.scope_and_question: Early viability was demonstrated by interventions including the introduction of the R21/Matrix-M vaccination and AI-assisted clinical decision support.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We conducted a thorough search for research published between April 2023 and September 2025 in the PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, PMC, and WHO databases.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Displacement, decreased functionality of medical facilities, and disruption of vector control were important factors.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The Sudanese conflict has significantly changed the operating environment for disease control since April 2023.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: To handle the changing burden, context-adapted methods are needed.

analysis.summary_en: Early viability was demonstrated by interventions including the introduction of the R21/Matrix-M vaccination and AI-assisted clinical decision support. We conducted a thorough search for research published between April 2023 and September 2025 in the PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, PMC, and WHO databases. Displacement, decreased functionality of medical facilities, and disruption of vector control were important factors. The Sudanese conflict has significantly changed the operating environment for disease control since April 2023. To handle the changing burden, context-adapted methods are needed.

title: A robust kinetic theory-based model for dengue transmission integrating climatic and socio-economic dynamics

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue is one of the most critical mosquito-borne viral diseases that has rapidly spread in recent years. Despite the fact that the first dengue vaccine was licensed in 2015, the vaccine is still in the experimental stage.
analysis.study_design_and_population: To capture realistic disease dynamics, two socio-economic events have been included: the large-scale cleaning and fogging campaign in 2018 following the 2017 outbreak, and reduced mobility during the COVID-19 restrictions in 2020.
analysis.methods: Methods In this study, we focus on developing a kinetic-based, data-driven quasi-equilibrium IR model incorporating controlling events along with weekly reported dengue cases, rainfall, temperature, and humidity, with specific time lags for each variable.
analysis.main_results: The simulated dengue incidence patterns closely matched reported data from 2016 to 2024, with accuracy levels ranging from 65% to 100% across different years. Comparison with a traditional kinetic SIR model showed negligible differences in infected host populations, indicating robust qualitative and quantitative agreement.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Its high accuracy highlights its usefulness for planning effective control strategies, especially in settings where vaccine coverage remains limited.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The proposed model offers a reliable framework for predicting dengue transmission by integrating climatic, vector-related, and human behavioral factors.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study design.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a kinetic theory-based model for dengue transmission that integrates climatic and socio-economic dynamics. The research aimed to address the need for improved understanding of dengue spread to design effective prevention strategies. The model was developed using a quasi-equilibrium IR approach, incorporating weekly dengue cases, rainfall, temperature, and humidity with specific time lags. The simulated dengue incidence patterns closely matched reported data from 2016 to 2024, with accuracy levels ranging from 65% to 100%. The model also showed negligible differences compared to a traditional SIR model, indicating robust agreement. The high accuracy of the model underscores its potential for informing control strategies, particularly in areas with limited vaccine coverage. The study's design included socio-economic events such as a cleaning campaign and reduced mobility during the pandemic. However, the evidence does not explicitly report limitations of the study design.

title: Clinical and Molecular Associations of Il-1β, Tnf-α, and Il-8 Polymorphisms in Dengue Patients

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue is a major arboviral disease where polymorphisms in genes encoding inflammatory mediators may modulate the immune response to dengue virus (DENV) infection. This study aimed to investigate the association of IL-1β rs1143634, IL-8 rs4073, and TNF-α rs361525 polymorphisms with susceptibility to DENV infection and with clinical manifestations and laboratory parameters.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case-control study was conducted in Goiânia, Goiás, Brazil, including individuals with confirmed DENV infection. The study included individuals with confirmed DENV infection and evaluated clinical and laboratory data according to genotype.
analysis.methods: Genomic IL-1β rs1143634, IL-8 rs4073, and TNF-α rs361525 polymorphisms were genotyped using TaqMan assays and real-time PCR. Logistic regression, Fisher's exact test, and Student's t-test were used for statistical analyses.
analysis.main_results: No significant association was observed between the evaluated polymorphisms and susceptibility to DENV infection (p > 0.05). However, the IL-8 rs4073 polymorphism was significantly associated with serum aminotransferase levels, AST (p = 0.002) and ALT (p = 0.040). The TNF-α rs361525 polymorphism was significantly associated with platelet count (p = 0.015) and IL-1β rs1143634 was significantly associated with low back pain (p = 0.040).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The association between IL-8 rs4073 and AST and ALT levels suggests a potential role of this polymorphism in hepatic involvement during dengue. Furthermore, the association of TNF-α rs361525 with thrombocytopenia and IL-1β rs1143634 with low back pain further supports the potential contribution of inflammatory genetic variants to the clinical heterogeneity of dengue.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that genetic polymorphisms may influence specific clinical features of dengue, which could inform future research on the genetic basis of disease severity and guide personalized approaches to diagnosis and treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Larger studies are required for underlying biological mechanisms. The supplied evidence does not report on the generalizability of the findings or potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association of IL-1β rs1143634, IL-8 rs4073, and TNF-α rs361525 polymorphisms with susceptibility to DENV infection and clinical manifestations. A case-control study was conducted in Goiânia, Brazil, using TaqMan assays and real-time PCR to genotype these polymorphisms. Statistical analyses included logistic regression, Fisher's exact test, and Student's t-test. The results showed no significant association with susceptibility or overall clinical symptoms, but IL-8 rs4073 was linked to elevated AST and ALT levels, TNF-α rs361525 with thrombocytopenia, and IL-1β rs1143634 with low back pain. These findings suggest a potential role of these polymorphisms in hepatic involvement and clinical heterogeneity during dengue. The study highlights the need for larger investigations to explore underlying mechanisms. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the limited sample size and the absence of detailed confounding controls.

title: A multiplex serological survey highlights differences in population immunity to mosquito-borne diseases in Vanuatu, Pacific region, 2023.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mosquito-borne pathogens are major emerging diseases and a growing public health concern in the Pacific, with occurrences linked to global increases, climate change and human mobility.
analysis.study_design_and_population: To support risk assessment of arboviruses and malaria in Vanuatu, a seroprevalence survey was conducted on Espiritu Santo Island, Efate Island, Malekula Island and Tanna Island between October 2022 and May 2023.
analysis.methods: Serum samples from 1,120 healthy participants aged 6-84 were tested for IgG against multiple arboviruses and malaria antigens using a multiplex microsphere immunoassay.
analysis.main_results: Standardized seroprevalence (IgG) reached 34% for dengue virus (DENV), 3.2% for Zika virus (ZIKV), 8.6% for Ross River virus (RRV), 4.4% for Plasmodium falciparum, and 36% for Plasmodium vivax.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Significant differences were observed between islands for ZIKV and P. vivax, and between age groups for DENV, RRV, and P.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results suggest silent circulation of RRV, consistent with findings in Fiji and French Polynesia, and confirm ongoing malaria transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: In a context of climate change and rapid spread of infectious diseases, our data suggest a significant risk for Vanuatu's population if pathogens were introduced.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a multiplex serological survey in Vanuatu to assess population immunity to mosquito-borne diseases, including dengue virus (DENV). The survey, carried out between October 2022 and May 2023, involved 1,120 healthy participants from four islands. The results showed that seroprevalence for DENV was 34%, while it was very rare or absent for other related viruses such as Zika, West Nile, Japanese Encephalitis, and Yellow fever. The findings highlight the silent circulation of Ross River virus and ongoing malaria transmission, suggesting a potential risk for Vanuatu's population if new pathogens are introduced. The study's results are relevant for understanding local immunity patterns and informing public health strategies in the context of climate change and increasing infectious disease spread.

title: Association of NS1 Antigen, IgM/IgG Antibodies with Haematological Indices and Inflammatory Markers in Suspected Dengue Cases: A Cross-sectional Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue Virus (DENV) has been re-emerging as a major public health challenge in tropical and subtropical regions, including India, with increasing incidence, changing epidemiology, and seasonal outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted from March 2025 to December 2025 at Adarsh Multispecialty Hospital, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India. The study included 154 patients presenting with Acute Febrile Illness (AFI).
analysis.methods: DENV diagnosis was performed using an immunochromatographic kit for NS1 antigen and IgM and IgG antibodies from the serum sample. Haematological indices, Inflammation markers and liver function tests Serum Glutamic Pyruvic Transaminase (SGPT) and Serum Glutamic Oxaloacetic Transaminase (SGOT) were examined.
analysis.main_results: A total of 154 suspected Dengue Fever (DF) samples were collected, out of which 38 cases of dengue infection were confirmed. The highest positivity was seen in the age group of 21 to 30 years, 14 (36.8%), with males being more affected, making up 24 (63.2%) of the cases. Liver enzymes were also elevated (SGOT 161.58±372.46 U/L and SGPT 187.46±456.09 U/L). They also showed raised C-Reactive Protein (CRP) in 33/38 (86.8%) of cases and higher Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) in 23/38 (60.5%) of cases.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Detection of the NS1 antigen with antibody testing gives more specific results. Integrated haematological, and inflammatory markers facilitate efficient risk stratification and enhance early dengue identification, enabling prompt clinical therapy during periods of peak transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Significant increase in CRP levels and a drop in platelet levels in dengue-positive patients are early indicators of presumptive diagnosis. Integrated haematological and inflammatory markers can enhance early dengue identification and support prompt clinical therapy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations. The evidence strength is high as the study provides specific associations between serological markers and clinical parameters in dengue infection.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate the association of serological markers with haematological, biochemical, and inflammatory parameters in clinically suspected dengue cases. Conducted at Adarsh Multispecialty Hospital in Gujarat, India, from March to December 2025, the study included 154 patients with acute febrile illness. DENV was diagnosed using an immunochromatographic kit for NS1 antigen and IgM/IgG antibodies. Among the 154 samples, 38 were confirmed as dengue infections, with the highest positivity in the 21–30 age group and males being more affected. Dengue patients showed significantly decreased platelet and white blood cell counts, as well as elevated liver enzymes and inflammatory markers like CRP and ESR. The authors concluded that combining NS1 antigen testing with antibody testing improves diagnostic specificity, and integrated haematological and inflammatory markers can aid in early diagnosis and risk stratification. The findings suggest that these markers could be valuable for early detection and prompt clinical management during peak transmission periods.

title: Haplotype diversity and variant switching associated with long-term transmission and outbreak dynamics of Dengue virus 3 genotype III lineages

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue viruses (DENV) evolve rapidly, resulting in highly diverse virus populations with varying epidemic potential. Even though DENV lineage replacement events are common in hyperendemic regions, often associated with outbreaks, the underlying fine-scale evolutionary processes are not well-described.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We analysed 5,443 inter-host envelope gene consensus sequences and 171 complete genomes of DENV-3 genotype III collected weekly in Singapore between 2015 and 2025.
analysis.methods: These datasets were analysed (i) to characterize the temporal dynamics of population structure from clades to haplotypes (ii) to determine unique genetic features and selection pressure and (iii) to infer the correlation between haplotype diversity and reported case numbers and vector abundance.
analysis.main_results: There were two distinct lineages (3III_B.1 [clade III] and 3III_B.3 [clade V]) that established long-term transmission, overlapping two outbreaks in 2019–2020 and 2022. The dominant variant of clade III showed the highest number of haplotypes and accumulated non-synonymous substitutions in a step-ladder pattern, whereas that of clade V maintained a less pronounced evolutionary profile during the study period. The overall haplotype diversity peaked during high transmission periods, in parallel to abundance of the vectors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Clade V was more common than clade III in 2019–2020 and was displaced by clade III in 2021, expanding exponentially during the 2022 outbreak. Despite variant diversity, only a single variant of each clade was dominant during respective outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance and risk assessment strategies by highlighting the relationship between haplotype diversity and outbreak dynamics. They also provide insights into the evolutionary patterns of DENV-3 genotype III, which may aid in understanding its transmission and potential for causing epidemics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations in the study design or analysis. The evidence strength is moderate, as the study is based on sequence data and does not include direct clinical or epidemiological outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the long-term transmission and outbreak dynamics of Dengue virus 3 (DENV-3) genotype III lineages in Singapore between 2015 and 2025. It analyzes 5,443 envelope gene consensus sequences and 171 complete genomes to explore the temporal dynamics of population structure, genetic features, selection pressure, and the correlation between haplotype diversity and reported case numbers and vector abundance. The results reveal two distinct lineages, clade III and clade V, which overlapped two outbreaks. Clade V was more prevalent in 2019–2020 but was displaced by clade III in 2021, which then expanded during the 2022 outbreak. The dominant variant of clade III showed a higher number of haplotypes and accumulated non-synonymous substitutions in a step-ladder pattern, while clade V had a less pronounced evolutionary profile. Haplotype diversity peaked during high transmission periods, aligning with vector abundance. The study provides insights into the evolutionary mechanisms of DENV-3 genotype III and their implications for outbreak dynamics, but it does not include direct clinical or epidemiological outcomes, limiting its evidence strength to moderate.

title: Supportive care and herbal interventions in dengue fever: A critical appraisal of hydration, nutrition, and plant-based therapies

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on dengue fever, a mosquito-borne viral disease caused by dengue viruses 1–4. The central question is to critically evaluate the evidence for natural and supportive management strategies, including oral hydration, nutritional support, rest, non-pharmacological symptom relief, and selected herbal interventions, in the context of dengue infection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a focused narrative review of clinical, preclinical, systematic-review, and guideline-based literature. It does not report specific databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria, but it includes a general description of the literature sources and review approach.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that oral hydration is the most established supportive measure for uncomplicated dengue. Nutritional support and rest may aid recovery, but there is no definitive evidence that herbal interventions, such as Carica papaya leaf extract, improve clinical outcomes like reduced bleeding, shock, hospitalization, or mortality.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence for other ethnomedicinal plants remains limited and largely preclinical. There is no consistent translation of improved platelet counts from Carica papaya leaf extract into better clinical outcomes. The review highlights the need for further well-designed trials to clarify the efficacy, safety, dosing, and standardization of herbal interventions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Natural approaches may be useful only as adjuncts to standard supportive care and should not replace clinical monitoring or timely referral. Further well-designed trials are needed to clarify efficacy, safety, dosing, and standardization of herbal interventions in dengue fever.

analysis.summary_en: This review critically evaluates natural and supportive management strategies for dengue fever, focusing on oral hydration, nutritional support, rest, and selected herbal interventions. It highlights that oral hydration is the most established supportive measure, while other interventions, such as Carica papaya leaf extract, show promise in improving platelet counts but lack consistent evidence of better clinical outcomes. The review emphasizes the need for well-designed trials to assess the efficacy and safety of herbal interventions. It concludes that natural approaches should complement, not replace, standard supportive care and clinical monitoring.

title: Entomological investigation of dengue outbreak in Raigarh, central India: Dominance of Aedes albopictus as the primary vector.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue outbreaks pose a significant public health threat in Raigarh city, central India. The study aimed to address the need for understanding the vector dynamics during a marked rise in febrile cases resembling dengue across urban areas.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An entomological survey was conducted in 16 wards of Raigarh city during the 2023-2024 rainy season. The study incorporated epidemiological data spanning nine years (2016-2024), along with a detailed month-wise analysis of dengue cases reported in 2023 and 2024.
analysis.methods: Vector density was assessed with House Index (HI), Container Index (CI), and Breteau Index (BI), to identify high-risk areas and predominant vector species. The study also involved identifying water-holding containers across 622 surveyed properties for vector breeding.
analysis.main_results: A total of 2080 water-holding containers were identified across 622 surveyed properties, for vector breeding. Among these, 67 (35%) were routinely used as household containers, while 124 (65%) were disposable items. Larval collections yielded 986 Aedes specimens, including 104 pupae, with Aedes albopictus accounting for 85% of the total, followed by Aedes aegypti (8%) and Aedes vittatus (5%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish Aedes albopictus as the predominant dengue vector in the region, alongside Aedes aegypti. The entomological indices reflected a critical vector proliferation scenario, with HI of 17.35%, CI of 7%, and BI of 24.49.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides critical insights into the vector dynamics of dengue in Raigarh, central India, which can inform targeted surveillance and intervention strategies to mitigate disease transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations to the study design or methodology. The evidence strength is moderate due to the focus on entomological indices and larval collections without detailed statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the dengue outbreak in Raigarh, central India, during the 2023-2024 rainy season. The research aimed to identify the primary vector species responsible for the outbreak and assess the entomological indices to guide intervention strategies. An entomological survey was conducted in 16 wards, identifying 2080 water-holding containers across 622 properties. Larval collections revealed that Aedes albopictus was the predominant vector, accounting for 85% of the specimens, followed by Aedes aegypti (8%) and Aedes vittatus (5%). The entomological indices indicated a critical vector proliferation scenario, with a House Index of 17.35%, Container Index of 7%, and Breteau Index of 24.49. The findings establish Aedes albopictus as the primary vector in the region, highlighting the need for targeted surveillance and community awareness programs. The study's evidence strength is moderate, as it focuses on entomological data without detailed statistical analysis.

title: Unlocking the antiviral potential of chalcones: A computational approach against dengue virus NS5 Protein.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify potential chalcone-based inhibitors of the NS5 methyltransferase domain of dengue virus due to the global health challenge posed by the absence of effective antiviral therapies for dengue virus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved docking 40 chalcone derivatives from the PubChem database against the NS5 methyltransferase domain of dengue virus (PDB ID: 6KR2).
analysis.methods: Chalcones were docked against the NS5 methyltransferase domain, evaluated for drug-likeness and toxicity, and their electronic properties were assessed using DFT.
analysis.main_results: Six chalcones showed better binding affinities than the reference ligand S-adenosylhomo-cysteine, with BL-3 emerging as the most promising due to its strong binding, safety profile, and electronic properties.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: BL-3 was interpreted as showing strong potential as an NS5 methyltransferase inhibitor and was recommended for further lead optimization and experimental validation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: BL-3 could be a candidate anti-DENV agent, potentially contributing to the development of new antiviral therapies for dengue virus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of computational methods and the need for experimental validation, and the sample size is small.

analysis.summary_en: This study identified potential chalcone-based inhibitors of the NS5 methyltransferase domain of dengue virus through computational methods, with BL-3 emerging as the most promising candidate for further development.

title: Fractional mathematical modeling of dengue fever (DF) in Afar region, Ethiopia

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the impact of asymptomatic and hospitalized individuals on the dynamic behavior of dengue fever. Dengue virus remains a significant global public health concern due to its transmission by female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study presents a fractional mathematical model of dengue fever dynamics with harmonic-type incidence, using real dengue data obtained from Afar Regional State of Ethiopia. The model focuses on the temporal evolution of all compartments to understand and predict the disease's behavior.
analysis.methods: The model was estimated by fitting it to real dengue data from Ethiopia. Fundamental mathematical analysis was conducted to confirm essential model properties, including the well-posedness of the solution.
analysis.main_results: The model was fitted to real dengue data from Ethiopia, allowing an in-depth analysis of epidemic trends. The simulation results indicate that vector control is mandatory because silent spread can have high mosquito infectivity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as highlighting the necessity of vector control to mitigate the risk of silent spread contributing to high mosquito infectivity. This study introduces a fractional mathematical model with harmonic-type incidence to better understand dengue fever dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for surveillance and control of dengue fever in Ethiopia. They emphasize the importance of vector control in preventing silent spread and reducing mosquito infectivity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a mathematical model fitted to real data, which may have limitations in capturing all real-world complexities. The evidence is moderate as it relies on model-based simulations and does not include direct empirical observations.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a fractional mathematical model of dengue fever dynamics with harmonic-type incidence to investigate the impact of asymptomatic and hospitalized individuals on the disease's behavior. The model was fitted to real dengue data from Afar Regional State, Ethiopia, to analyze epidemic trends. The simulation results emphasize the necessity of vector control due to the potential for silent spread to increase mosquito infectivity. The authors interpret these findings as highlighting the importance of understanding and predicting dengue fever dynamics for effective public health interventions. The study's significance lies in its contribution to modeling approaches for dengue surveillance and control. However, the evidence is moderate, as the study relies on model-based simulations rather than direct empirical data.

title: CD5L as a potential immunomodulator in dengue severity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate serum CD5L levels in dengue-infected individuals and investigate its association with serological markers and disease severity. CD5L is a secreted glycoprotein involved in immune regulation, macrophage polarization, and lipid metabolism, but its role in dengue virus infection remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study involving dengue-positive and dengue-negative individuals was conducted to compare serum CD5L concentrations and assess correlations with NS1, IgM, IgG status, and disease severity.
analysis.methods: Serum samples were collected from confirmed dengue-positive patients and dengue-negative controls. CD5L concentrations were quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and analyzed according to serological profiles (NS1, IgM, and IgG). Two-group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test, and multiple groups were analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's post hoc test. A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
analysis.main_results: CD5L levels were significantly elevated in dengue-positive individuals compared to dengue-negative controls (p < 0.05), with the highest levels observed in IgG-positive only individuals (p <0.001). No significant differences were seen in NS1-positive only or IgM-positive only groups, suggesting that CD5L upregulation is associated with IgG seropositivity rather than acute-phase markers. Among IgG-positive only individuals, CD5L levels were significantly higher in non-severe dengue cases compared to severe dengue cases (p <0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This study highlights CD5L's potential role in dengue pathogenesis, particularly its association with IgG seropositivity and non-severe disease. Further research is needed to clarify its mechanisms and evaluate its potential as a biomarker or therapeutic target in dengue virus infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a potential association between increased CD5L and later stages of dengue virus infection with less severe outcomes. This could inform future studies on CD5L as a biomarker or therapeutic target in dengue virus infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which does not establish causality. The sample size and lack of longitudinal data may also affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated serum CD5L levels in dengue-infected individuals and found that CD5L was significantly elevated in dengue-positive cases, particularly in IgG-positive individuals. CD5L levels were higher in non-severe dengue cases compared to severe cases, suggesting a potential role in dengue pathogenesis and disease severity.

title: MicroRNA Responses Associated with Vector-Borne Diseases in Humans and Arthropod Vectors: A Systematic Review

analysis.scope_and_question: This systematic review surveys research conducted on miRNA responses in disease vectors and human hosts of VBDs. Vector-borne diseases (VBDs) represent a significant public health challenge.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic search of four databases and manual searching identified 93 qualifying articles. The review includes studies on miRNA responses in both human hosts and arthropod vectors of VBDs.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Twenty-eight in vivo human studies have characterised miRNAs linked to VBDs, including dengue. Some overlaps of miRNA responses to infection were observed for Chagas disease (miR-208a), dengue (miR-146-5p), and schistosomiasis (sma-miR-bantam), while the majority exhibited minimal overlap.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report specific controversies or evidence gaps related to dengue virus. However, it notes a paucity of studies investigating miRNA biomarkers for VBD diagnosis and prognosis in humans.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: This review reports a paucity of studies investigating miRNA biomarkers for VBD diagnosis and prognosis in humans and nominates the development of standardised protocols and validation across study cohorts as future directions.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review explores miRNA responses in human hosts and arthropod vectors of vector-borne diseases (VBDs), with a focus on dengue virus. The review identifies 93 qualifying articles and highlights the role of miRNAs as potential biomarkers for disease diagnosis. While some miRNA overlaps were observed for dengue and other VBDs, the majority of responses were distinct. The review underscores the need for more research on miRNA biomarkers for dengue and calls for standardised protocols and validation across study cohorts to improve diagnostic accuracy and disease management.

title: A Data‐Driven Approach to Predicting Dengue Fever

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue has emerged as a critical global health challenge, contributing to increasing mortality rates and exerting substantial pressure on healthcare systems.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In this study, we develop a machine learning–based approach using Random Forest regression to predict weekly dengue cases for the cities of San Juan (Puerto Rico) and Iquitos (Peru).
analysis.methods: In recent years, machine learning (ML) algorithms have emerged as valuable tools for analyzing complex datasets and predicting disease patterns. Our model leverages weather, satellite, and vegetation index data to forecast disease incidence, with missing data handled through preprocessing and feature engineering.
analysis.main_results: A noteworthy finding was the superior performance of a variant of SVM, namely, PCA-SVM (poly-5), which achieved an accuracy of 99.52%, sensitivity of 99.75%, and specificity of 99.09%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings underscore the promising role of machine learning in enhancing diagnostic precision for dengue.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The high-performance metrics reported in several studies suggest that ML-based approaches could serve as effective clinical decision support tools.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Future research should focus on validation across larger, diverse datasets and real-world clinical settings to ensure robustness, generalizability, and practical applicability.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a data-driven approach to predicting dengue fever using machine learning techniques. Dengue has become a significant global health challenge, prompting research into advanced diagnostic methods. The study employs Random Forest regression to forecast weekly dengue cases in San Juan and Iquitos, utilizing weather, satellite, and vegetation index data. A variant of support vector machines, PCA-SVM (poly-5), demonstrated high accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity in diagnosing dengue. The findings highlight the potential of machine learning in improving diagnostic precision for dengue. The model's performance is evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and the study emphasizes the need for further validation in diverse and real-world settings to ensure its reliability and applicability. The results suggest that ML-based approaches could be valuable tools for clinical decision support and public health interventions.

title: EHD4 facilitates Zika virus infection by regulating extracellular vesicle-associated viral release and cell attachment.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of host factors in regulating the composition and infectivity of extracellular vesicle-associated viral material, particularly in the context of dengue virus infection, as the mechanisms governing this process remain incompletely understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used genetic ablation and re-expression of EHD4 in HeLa cells to assess its impact on the propagation of dengue virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, and ZIKV. It also examined ZIKV-infected EHD4-knockout and wild-type cells to compare extracellular viral RNA distribution.
analysis.methods: EHD4 was genetically ablated in HeLa cells, and its effects on viral propagation were tested using genetic re-expression. The study also performed comparative proteomic profiling, immunofluorescence, and transmission electron microscopy to analyze the role of EHD4 in viral sorting and extracellular vesicle composition.
analysis.main_results: Genetic ablation of EHD4 impaired the propagation of dengue virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, and ZIKV, while re-expression restored viral propagation. In ZIKV-infected EHD4-knockout cells, a greater proportion of extracellular viral RNA was found in EV-enriched fractions compared to wild-type cells.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that EHD4 plays a critical role in regulating the extracellular partitioning, composition, and infectivity of flaviviral material, particularly in EV-enriched fractions, highlighting a novel host-virus interaction mechanism.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the host factors that influence viral dissemination and infectivity, which could inform strategies for targeting viral spread and improving diagnostic or therapeutic approaches for dengue and related flaviviruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study primarily used in vitro models and did not include in vivo data, which may limit the generalizability of findings. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on abstract-only data and does not provide detailed mechanistic insights.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of EHD4 in regulating the extracellular dissemination and infectivity of flaviviruses, including dengue virus. Using genetic ablation and re-expression in HeLa cells, the research shows that EHD4 is essential for viral propagation and influences the composition and infectivity of extracellular vesicle-associated viral material. The findings suggest EHD4 facilitates viral sorting into MVB luminal vesicles, impacting viral release and cell attachment. While the study provides novel insights into host-virus interactions, its reliance on in vitro models and lack of in vivo data limit the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on abstract-only data and does not fully elucidate the molecular mechanisms involved.

title: Strain-Dependent Cross-Neutralization of Closely Related Asian-Lineage Zika Viruses by Dengue-Immune Sera

analysis.research_question_and_background: Zika virus (ZIKV) and dengue virus (DENV) co-circulate in tropical regions and elicit cross-reactive immunity. However, differential neutralization of closely related ZIKV strains remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study characterizes the neutralization profiles of dengue-immune sera against DENV and two Asian-lineage ZIKV strains, P6-740 and PRVABC59. Sera from suspected dengue infections and from healthy donors were screened for anti-DENV IgM and IgG antibodies and anti-ZIKV IgM and IgG antibodies by ELISA and grouped.
analysis.methods: Neutralization against DENV serotypes and two ZIKV strains was quantified using the foci reduction neutralization test (FRNT). Neutralization was also detected in some ELISA-seronegative samples. Complete genome sequences of ZIKV P6-740 and PRVABC59 were compared to identify amino acid differences.
analysis.main_results: Sera containing anti-DENV IgG showed higher neutralizing activity against both DENV and ZIKV than IgG-negative sera. Across all immunological groups, neutralization titers were higher against ZIKV P6-740 than ZIKV PRVABC59. Four amino acid substitutions were identified in the envelope (E) protein.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Dengue-induced immunity differentially neutralizes closely related ZIKV strains, with generally stronger activity against P6-740, suggesting that viral genetic variation may influence cross-neutralization outcomes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that viral genetic variation may influence cross-neutralization outcomes, which could inform surveillance and diagnostic strategies for ZIKV in dengue-endemic regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, which may not capture full context. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on serological and genomic data without detailed clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the differential neutralization of closely related Asian-lineage Zika viruses by dengue-immune sera. It highlights that dengue-induced immunity shows stronger neutralizing activity against ZIKV P6-740 than PRVABC59, suggesting that viral genetic variation may impact cross-neutralization. The findings have implications for understanding immune responses in tropical regions where both viruses co-circulate. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence, which limits the depth of analysis and suggests a moderate confidence level in the results.

title: Medicine–food homology and related natural products against mosquito-borne viruses: pharmacological evidence, mechanisms and translational priorities

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on Dengue virus (DENV) and related entities such as Zika virus (ZIKV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), which cause substantial morbidity. The central question is about the potential of medicine–food homology (MFH) materials and related natural products as sources of antiviral agents against these viruses, with an emphasis on distinguishing purified compounds from extracts, sulfated polysaccharides and semi-synthetic derivatives.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a critical narrative review that examines the antiviral evidence, mechanisms and prospects for translation of MFH materials and related natural products. It includes a range of study designs, with some candidates evaluated in animals and others relying on cellular activity and biochemical or pathway-perturbation evidence.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that reported effects of MFH materials and related natural products span virion inactivation, entry, replication and maturation, as well as host pathways involving interferon responses, oxidative stress, inflammation and lipid metabolism. It also emphasizes the importance of defined composition, reproducible infectious-virus readouts and an exposure profile compatible with their intended use.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The main development gaps concern reproducibility, selectivity and whether active concentrations can be reached in the tissues relevant to each infection. Additionally, clinical antiviral benefit has not been established for the candidates reviewed, indicating a lack of definitive evidence for their therapeutic efficacy.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Priority should be given to candidates with defined composition, reproducible infectious-virus readouts and an exposure profile compatible with their intended use. This approach supports the development of direct antivirals, host-directed treatments and supportive interventions while keeping their distinct therapeutic claims clear.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the potential of medicine–food homology (MFH) materials and related natural products as antiviral agents against Dengue virus (DENV) and related mosquito-borne viruses. It highlights the diverse chemical scaffolds these materials offer and their reported effects on viral processes and host pathways. However, the review notes that clinical antiviral benefits have not been established, and development gaps include reproducibility, selectivity and achieving active concentrations in relevant tissues. The implications suggest prioritizing candidates with defined composition and reproducible evidence for their therapeutic use.

title: An Adaptive Gated Fusion-based Multimodal Framework for Influential Actor Identification in Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever Information Dissemination on YouTube

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue hemorrhagic fever remains a critical public health concern in Indonesia, and YouTube has become a major channel for health information. Identifying influential actors is essential for public health communication, yet existing social network analysis relies on text and ignores visual signals such as video thumbnails.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study proposes a multimodal framework based on Adaptive Gated Fusion that combines text and visual features without any audio modality. Textual features from IndoBERT and visual features from ResNet-50 are fused adaptively per dimension, aggregated per channel, and used to build a content-based co-audience network analysed with PageRank.
analysis.methods: Using 33,233 Indonesian comments from 5,365 videos across 1,129 collected channels (1,084 retained after language filtering) over 2021 to 2025, an ablation study with stratified five-fold cross-validation shows the fused representation reaches 79.52 percent accuracy and 78.42 percent macro F1, outperforming text and visual baselines.
analysis.main_results: KOMPASTV, Kata Dokter, and Halodoc emerged as the most influential actors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that their framework effectively identifies influential actors in dengue hemorrhagic fever information dissemination on YouTube by integrating both text and visual features, which is a novel approach compared to existing methods that rely solely on text.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for monitoring and managing dengue hemorrhagic fever information on social media platforms like YouTube, helping to target influential actors for more effective health communication.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to YouTube data from Indonesia and relies on user comments, which may not fully represent the broader discourse. The evidence strength is moderate due to the focus on a single platform and region.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces an adaptive gated fusion-based multimodal framework for identifying influential actors in dengue hemorrhagic fever information dissemination on YouTube. The framework integrates both textual and visual features, using IndoBERT for text and ResNet-50 for visual analysis. The study analyzed 33,233 Indonesian comments from 5,365 videos across 1,129 channels, with 1,084 retained after language filtering. Results showed the framework achieved 79.52 percent accuracy and 78.42 percent macro F1, outperforming text and visual baselines. KOMPASTV, Kata Dokter, and Halodoc were identified as the most influential actors. The study highlights the importance of incorporating visual signals in social network analysis for public health communication. However, the findings are limited to YouTube data from Indonesia and rely on user comments, which may not capture the full scope of health information dissemination. The evidence strength is moderate due to the regional and platform-specific focus.

title: Clinical and Laboratory Profile of Dengue Cases in a Tertiary Care Hospital, Dhaka

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the clinical profile and laboratory findings of dengue patients presenting to a tertiary care hospital in Dhaka, Bangladesh, due to recent distinct epidemiological patterns of dengue outbreaks in the region.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted from February to December 2025 in the Department of Medicine, Tairunnessa Memorial Medical College & Hospital, Dhaka, Bangladesh, involving 100 dengue patients.
analysis.methods: Ethical approval was obtained, and written informed consent was secured from all participants. Laboratory tests including complete blood count, liver function tests, renal function tests, NS1 antigen, and dengue IgM/IgG serology were performed. Data were analyzed using statistical tests.
analysis.main_results: The study observed that 65% of patients had a p-value 1, indicating a significant association with certain clinical parameters.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as establishing diagnosis based on clinical and laboratory parameters, highlighting the importance of these tests in dengue management.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance and diagnosis of dengue in the region, aiding in timely intervention and management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and small sample size, which may affect generalizability. Ethical approval and informed consent were obtained, and statistical tests were used for analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the clinical and laboratory profile of dengue patients in Dhaka, Bangladesh, from February to December 2025. It involved 100 patients and found significant associations with certain clinical parameters, emphasizing the importance of diagnostic tests.

title: Retinal Vascular Complications of Dengue Fever, an Unexplored Entity:

analysis.research_question_and_background: Systemic manifestations of dengue fever are well characterised, however ocular involvement has historically been considered a rare and under-recognised complication.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Case Report: We describe a case series of five patients, all with clinically and serologically confirmed dengue fever who developed retinal vascular complications.
analysis.methods: Demographic data were extracted, along with systemic history (interval between dengue infection diagnosis to the onset of ocular symptoms, and interval between visual complaint to ophthalmic evaluation), and presenting best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA).
analysis.main_results: The mean interval between dengue fever diagnosis to the onset of visual symptoms was 9.6 days (range 7-14 days).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Dengue fever can produce a diverse spectrum of retinal vascular complications, typically manifesting one to three weeks after the onset of systemic illness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Prompt recognition and management is needed to avoid ocular complications and visual impairment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This case report explores the under-recognised retinal vascular complications of dengue fever, highlighting a diverse spectrum of ocular manifestations typically occurring one to three weeks after systemic illness onset. Five patients with confirmed dengue fever developed retinal vascular issues, including central retinal artery occlusion, Purtscher-like retinopathy, paracentral acute-middle maculopathy (PAMM), and branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO). The mean interval between dengue diagnosis and visual symptoms was 9.6 days. Spectral-domain OCT is emphasized as a critical diagnostic tool, even when clinical findings are inconspicuous. The study underscores the importance of early detection and management to prevent visual impairment. However, the evidence is limited to a single case series, which may not fully represent the broader population or long-term outcomes.

title: Meteorological predictors of dengue hemorrhagic fever incidence in Cilacap Regency, Indonesia: A time series analysis

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to analyze the nonlinear relationship between meteorological predictors and dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) incidence, and to quantify the meteorologically attributable fraction of DHF during 2021-2025 in Cilacap Regency, Indonesia.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An ecological time series design was used, analyzing data from Cilacap Regency, Indonesia, between 2021 and 2025. The study included sequential three-stage analytical tools to assess the relationship between DHF and meteorological predictors.
analysis.methods: The study employed a cross-correlation function (CCF) analysis to identify lag structures, Granger causality within a vector autoregression (VAR) framework to confirm directional temporal precedence, and a quasi-Poisson Distributed Lag Nonlinear Model (DLNM) with natural cubic spline crossbases over a 28-day lag window to estimate the exposure-response relationship.
analysis.main_results: Granger causality testing confirmed unidirectional relationships between DHF and all four predictors, including mean temperature, rainfall, relative humidity, and wind speed (all P <0.05). Daily rainfall was the dominant predictor with a relative risk (RR) of 4.23 (95% CI 2.10-8.52) and an attributable fraction of 27.58%. The mean temperature showed a J-shaped exposure-response curve, with a protective nadir at 26.5°C and a markedly elevated risk above 28°C (RR 2.13; 95% CI 1.43-3.19; AF = 6.22%). Relative humidity (AF= -14.40%) and wind speed (AF= -3.37%) demonstrated complex nonlinear patterns contributing net protective attributable fractions. Overall, the model explained 52.26% of the null deviance (QAIC= 3984.23).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that rainfall and temperature were the meteorological predictors most strongly associated with DHF incidence in Cilacap Regency, highlighting the nonlinear relationship between these factors and DHF.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that incorporating meteorological predictors into vector control programs and early warning systems could help prevent DHF outbreaks in Cilacap Regency.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Autoregressive terms and long-term trends were included to account for autocorrelation and potential confounding, but the study's ecological design may limit the ability to infer individual-level causal relationships. The evidence is moderate as it is based on an abstract-only analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the relationship between meteorological predictors and dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) incidence in Cilacap Regency, Indonesia, using a time series analysis. The research aimed to quantify the meteorologically attributable fraction of DHF during 2021-2025. The ecological design incorporated sequential three-stage analytical tools, including cross-correlation function (CCF) analysis, Granger causality testing, and a quasi-Poisson Distributed Lag Nonlinear Model (DLNM). Results showed that daily rainfall was the dominant predictor with a relative risk of 4.23 (95% CI 2.10-8.52) and an attributable fraction of 27.58%. Mean temperature exhibited a J-shaped exposure-response curve, with a protective nadir at 26.5°C and elevated risk above 28°C (RR 2.13; 95% CI 1.43-3.19; AF = 6.22%). Relative humidity and wind speed showed net protective effects. The model explained 52.26% of the null deviance.
